fixes.explanation: Paul writes that "…God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus…" Titus worked alongside Paul (2 Corinthians 8:23). Notice who gets the credit. God is the one doing the comforting, and Titus is how it arrived.

Paul never mentions anything like that. He says Titus "…told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me…" Longing and zeal are the opposite of walking away. Nobody was hanging up the phone.

Paul says Titus told them about the Corinthians' longing, mourning and zeal, "…so that I rejoiced all the more." All the more, friend. He was already comforted, and then the joy kept growing. That's a batch that comes out of the oven bigger than it went in.
Titus's news brought the opposite. Paul says, "…so that I rejoiced all the more." The fears in Macedonia were real (2 Corinthians 7:5), but worry isn't the word here. Joy is.

Paul says, "…I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance." His joy isn't in the sorrow, friend. It's in where the sorrow led. That's a good father's heart.

Shame isn't where Paul says godly sorrow leads. He writes, "Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret…" The place it leads is salvation, and Paul says it comes without regret. Shame isn't in that sentence.
Peace isn't what Paul says worldly sorrow brings. He writes, "…but worldly sorrow brings death." I think that's a heavy line, friend. Godly sorrow is the one that leads to salvation.

Paul says he wrote "…that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God." He says it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed. He wanted them to see their own earnestness. I think that's a gift, friend.

Paul writes, "Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you." He also says "…our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well." That's a relief if you've ever bragged on somebody ahead of time.

Paul doesn't describe a hesitant welcome. He says Titus remembers "…you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling." Obedient is the word he picks. Doubts and questions aren't in his picture.

Pride and boasting aren't in Paul's picture here. He says Titus remembers "…you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling." Obedience and fear and trembling are what he names. And Titus's affection for them grew even greater.
